# Baseline Data Extraction

This file achieves the following goals:

1. Identification of concussion and uninjured children as of the baseline timepoint
2. Extraction of features values for those children

## Loading packages

The `abcdutils` package can be installed from GitHub using the command: `devtools::install_github("BRANCHlab/abcdutils")`.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(abcdutils)
library(visdat)
```

## Path set-up

The `path_maker()` function returns other functions that can turn relative paths into absolute ones.
The functions returned by `path_maker()` also have a `date` parameter which attach as a prefix the current date to a file name.

```{r}
core_path <- path_maker(here::here("data/abcd/core"))
input_path <- path_maker(here::here("data/abcd/inputs"))
sub_path <- path_maker(here::here("data/abcd/subjects"))
fig_path <- path_maker(here::here("data/abcd/results/figures"))

core_path <- path_maker(here::here("data/abcd/core"))
import <- function(path) {
    return(abcd_load(core_path(path)))
}
```

## Subject identification

All information required for identifying children at a chronic stage (> 3 months) following mTBI as of baseline data collection is available in the `ph_p_otbi.csv` file.
To identify subjects at a chronic stage post-mTBI, two intermediate pieces of information must be calculated from the original dataset:

* identifying which head injuries were mTBIs
* identifying the time since the most recent mTBI

The structure of the Ohio State TBI screen as used for ABCD data collection was not completely compatible with the most commonly used definition of mTBI [@blennow_traumatic_2016], which requires at least one of the following:

* Any period of loss of consciousness
* Any loss of memory
* Any alteration in mental state
* Focal neurological deficits

But none of the following:

* LOC over 30 minutes
* A Glasgow Coma Scale score below 13
* Post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) greater than 24 hours

A few aspects of the data collection process in the ABCD study precluded the usage of this definition:

* No information was collected regarding the GCS
* Feeling dazed and PTA were combined into a single variable, making it unclear which combination of symptoms was present
* No information was collected regarding the duration of feeling dazed or experiencing PTA

Consequently, I defined mTBI as any injury that resulted in **either**:

1. LOC for less than 30 minutes (including 0 minutes) **AND** any duration of memory loss / feeling dazed
2. LOC for less than 30 minutes but greater than 0 minutes

The fixed nature of the questionnaire also meant that some information about multiple mTBIs sustained in the same way or about a very large number of mTBIs throughout a child's life could have been lost (see the previous section on identifying children with a history of mTBI).
For my analyses, I assume these edge cases are not common enough to meaningfully change any obtained conclusions.

```{r}
# 11864 total children included in baseline TBI data
ph_p_otbi |>
    filter_timepoint(0) |>
    nrow()

# mTBI subjects (latest mTBI at least 3 months prior to baseline collection)
# N = 437
mtbi_subs <- get_mtbi_subjects(
    ph_p_otbi,
    abcd_y_lt,
    min_mpi = 3,
    t = 0
)

# Later analyses show some unusual data for subject: NDAR_INVBU31791C.
# They are removed from the uninjured subjects list.

# Uninjured subjects (those with no injuries as of baseline collection)
# N = 9349
unij_subs <- get_uninjured_subjects(
    ph_p_otbi,
    abcd_y_lt,
    t = 0
)

write_csv(mtbi_subs, sub_path("mtbi_subs.csv", date = TRUE))
write_csv(unij_subs, sub_path("unij_subs.csv", date = TRUE))
```

A chunk for building the sample criteri figure:

```{r}

# 11864
ph_p_otbi |>
    detail_mtbi(abcd_y_lt) |>
    filter_timepoint(0) |>
    nrow()

# 445
ph_p_otbi |>
    detail_mtbi(abcd_y_lt) |>
    filter_timepoint(0) |>
    dplyr::filter(mtbi == 1) |>
    dplyr::filter(
        moderate_tbi == 0 &
        severe_tbi == 0
    ) |>
    nrow()

# 437
ph_p_otbi |>
    detail_mtbi(abcd_y_lt) |>
    filter_timepoint(0) |>
    dplyr::filter(mtbi == 1) |>
    dplyr::filter(
        moderate_tbi == 0 &
        severe_tbi == 0
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(latest_mtbi_mpi >= 3) |>
    nrow()

mtbi_subs <- get_mtbi_subjects(
    ph_p_otbi,
    abcd_y_lt,
    min_mpi = 3,
    t = 0
)
```


```{r}
# CHECKPOINT
mtbi_subs <- read_subjects(sub_path("2025_07_31_mtbi_subs.csv"))
unij_subs <- read_subjects(sub_path("2025_07_31_unij_subs.csv"))

length(mtbi_subs)
length(unij_subs)
```

A few types of injuries were handled differently from the rest in the above code.
For the `other_loc` injury type, the questionnaire asked for a total number of injuries with LOC as well as a total number of injuries with LOC above 30 minutes.
If their difference was above 0, they were labelled as having had an mTBI.
For the `other_multi` and `other_other_multi` injury types, insufficient information was provided to determine the severity of the associated injuries.

## Extracting input variables

### Acute symptoms

The acute symptom data is found within the TBI dataset.
We are interesed in the following acute symptoms:

* mechanism of injury
* age
* LOC information
* Feeling dazed or having memory loss

A few more intermediate columns need to be added to isolate these variables for the most recent mTBIs of the subjects.

#### Feeling dazed

```{r}
mtbi_as_mem_daze <- get_mtbi_mem_daze(
    ph_p_otbi,
    abcd_y_lt,
    mtbi_subs,
    t = 0
)

dplyr::tibble(mtbi_as_mem_daze)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_as_mem_daze,
    input_path("mtbi_as_mem_daze.csv", date = TRUE)
)
```

#### Mechanism of injury

```{r}
mtbi_as_mechanism <- get_mtbi_mechanism(
    ph_p_otbi,
    abcd_y_lt,
    mtbi_subs,
    t = 0
)

tibble(mtbi_as_mechanism)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_as_mechanism,
    input_path("mtbi_as_mechanism.csv", date = TRUE)
)
```

#### Loss of consciousness

#### Household income

Income was coded as a 3-level variable. 
Here are some other ABCD studies looking at income:

- 10-levels
    - Tomasi 2021 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33990770/)
    - Rakesh 2021 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34419766/)
    - Guberman 2022 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35579325/)
- 6-levels
    - Nagata 2024 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38323959/)
- 3-levels
    - Nishat 2023 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37441978/)
    - Nishat 2024 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38237797/)
    - Cook 2021 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34790165/)
    - Veliz 2023 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36689685/)

### Neuroimaging

Variables of interest related to brain structure and function include:

* Structural: T1-weighted multishell diffusion-weighted MRI data
* Diffusion: Neurite density (restricted spectrum imaging)
* Functional: resting-state functional MRI data

[@hagler_image_2019] outlines the neuroimaging data present in the ABCD dataset in detail.

#### Structural MRI

The sMRI variables of interest include subcortical volumes, and cortical thicknesses, and cortical surface areas.

For cortical surface areas, the relevant file is abcd_mrisdp10201, which contains the cortical surface areas of ~150 regions (variables `mrisdp_*` where * ranges from 1 to 151).

For cortical thicknesses, the relevant file is abcd_mrisdp10201, which contains the cortical thickness of ~150 regions (variables `mrisdp_*` where * ranges from 303 to 453).

##### Subcortical volume

```{r}
mtbi_sm_subc_v <- get_subc_v(
    mri_y_smr_vol_aseg,
    mtbi_subs,
    t = 0,
    only_whole_brain = FALSE
)
dplyr::tibble(mtbi_sm_subc_v)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_sm_subc_v,
    input_path("mtbi_sm_subc_v.csv", date = TRUE)
)

unij_sm_subc_v <- get_subc_v(

)
```

##### Cortical thickness

Both the Desikan and Destrieux cortical parcellations could have been used for the cortical imaging data collected below.
A comparison between the two can be found in the appendix.
Because there happens to be a few more participants with calculated Desikan parcellations, that is what is used here.

#### Diffusion MRI

We are interested in the neurite density measures of white matter regions in the brain.
Previously, these measures were found in variables containing the string "rsindwm_cdk" within the file `mri_rsi_p102.txt`.
A change anounced in the ABCD 4.0 MRI release notes indicates that neurite density is now referred to as "restricted normalized directional" and that the relevant white matter variables contain the string "rsirndwm" within the file `abcd_drsip201.txt`.

##### White matter neurite densities

Some potential summary neurite density meeasures:

* dmri_rsirnd_fib_allfib (AtlasTrack fiber segmentation, all fibers)
* dmri_rsirndwm_cdk_mean (Desikan cortical parcellation peri-cortical white matter mean)

```{r}
# White matter neurite densities
mtbi_dm_wmnd <- get_wmnd(
    mri_y_rsi_rnd_at,
    mri_y_rsi_rnd_wm_dsk,
    subjects = mtbi_subs,
    t = 0,
    only_mean = FALSE
)
dplyr::tibble(mtbi_dm_wmnd)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_dm_wmnd,
    input_path("mtbi_dm_wmnd.csv", date = TRUE)
)

unij_dm_wmnd <- get_wmnd(
    mri_y_rsi_rnd_at,
    mri_y_rsi_rnd_wm_dsk,
    subjects = unij_subs,
    t = 0,
    only_mean = FALSE
)
dplyr::tibble(unij_dm_wmnd)

readr::write_csv(
    unij_dm_wmnd,
    input_path("unij_dm_wmnd.csv", date = TRUE)
)
```

#### Resting-state functional MRI

We are interested in the following rs-fMRI measures:

- Gordon network (cortical) correlations
- Subcortical correlations

frontoparietal network: _fo_ or _fopa_

default mode network: _df_ or _dt_

salience network: _sa_


##### Cortical parcellation network correlations

```{r}

mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_gp |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::contains(c("_dt_", "_sa_", "_fo_"))) |> colnames()

mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_aseg |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::contains(c("_df_", "_sa_", "_fopa_"))) |> colnames()

skimr::skim(mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_aseg)

mtbi_rm_gord_cor <- get_gord_cor(
    mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_gp,
    mtbi_subs,
    t = 0
)

colnames(mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_gp)


dplyr::tibble(mtbi_rm_gord_cor)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_rm_gord_cor,
    input_path("mtbi_rm_gord_cor.csv", date = TRUE)
)

unij_rm_gord_cor <- get_gord_cor(
    mri_y_rsfmr_cor_gp_gp,

readr::write_csv(

)
```

#### Healthy behaviours

#### Prosocial behaviour

```{r}
mtbi_p_prosocial_p <- get_prosocial_behaviour_p(
    ce_p_psb,
    mtbi_subs,
    no_zero = TRUE,
    t = 0
)

mtbi_p_prosocial_y <- get_prosocial_behaviour_y(
    ce_y_psb,
    mtbi_subs,
    no_zero = TRUE,
    t = 0
)

mtbi_p_prosocial <- dplyr::inner_join(
    mtbi_p_prosocial_y,
    mtbi_p_prosocial_p
)


dplyr::tibble(mtbi_p_prosocial)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_p_prosocial,
    input_path("mtbi_p_prosocial.csv", date = TRUE)
)

unij_p_prosocial_p <- get_prosocial_behaviour_p(
    ce_p_psb,
    unij_subs,
    no_zero = TRUE,
    t = 0
)

unij_p_prosocial_y <- get_prosocial_behaviour_y(
    ce_y_psb,
    unij_subs,
    no_zero = TRUE,
    t = 0
)

unij_p_prosocial <- dplyr::inner_join(
    unij_p_prosocial_p,
    unij_p_prosocial_y
)

dplyr::tibble(unij_p_prosocial)

readr::write_csv(
    unij_p_prosocial,
    input_path("unij_p_prosocial.csv", date = TRUE)
)
```

## Output variables

### Child Behaviour Checklist

CBCL syndrom subscales include anxious-depressed withdrawn-depressed, somatic complaints, social complaints, thought complaints, attention complaints, rulebreak complaints, and aggressive complaints.

```{r}
mtbi_cbcl <- get_cbcl_syndrome_scale(
    mh_p_cbcl,
    raw = TRUE,
    subjects = mtbi_subs,
    t = 0
)

dplyr::tibble(mtbi_cbcl)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_cbcl,
    input_path("mtbi_cbcl.csv", date = TRUE)
)

unij_cbcl <- get_cbcl_syndrome_scale(
    mh_p_cbcl,
    raw = TRUE,
    subjects = unij_subs,
    t = 0
)

dplyr::tibble(unij_cbcl)

readr::write_csv(
    unij_cbcl,

)
```

## Other covariates

### Scanner information

Note that there are 22 unique site values: https://neurostars.org/t/abcd-family-nested-within-site-or-scanner-id-how-to-deal-with-inaccuracies/18664

```{r}
set.seed(42)
mtbi_scanner <- get_scanner_id(
    mri_y_adm_info = mri_y_adm_info,
    subjects = mtbi_subs,
    t = 0,
    abcd_y_lt = abcd_y_lt,
    sample_missing = TRUE
)

dplyr::tibble(mtbi_scanner)

readr::write_csv(
    mtbi_scanner,
    input_path("mtbi_scanner.csv", date = TRUE)
)

set.seed(42)
unij_scanner <- get_scanner_id(
    mri_y_adm_info = mri_y_adm_info,
    subjects = unij_subs,
    t = 0,
    abcd_y_lt = abcd_y_lt,
    sample_missing = TRUE
)

dplyr::tibble(unij_scanner)

readr::write_csv(
    unij_scanner,
    input_path("unij_scanner.csv", date = TRUE)
)
```
